correctness.rationale: With y=v+w+z+t in consecutive exterior degrees, y^2=2v wedge w+w wedge w and y^3=0; z,t give q^5 free choices. In coordinates the Pfaffian of w is a dot product of (w12,w13,w14) with (w34,-w24,w23), so a fixed nonzero top component gives (q^3-1)q^2 bivectors. Each is nondegenerate and v maps isomorphically to degree three under v -> 2v wedge w. With zero top and nonzero cubic component, a nonzero decomposable w can occur exactly when its plane lies in the cubic's three-dimensional support. This gives (q-1)(q^2+q+1)=q^3-1 choices, each allowing q^2 vectors v. For zero target the pair count is q^4+q^2(q^2+1)(q^3-1), giving the stated zero fiber after multiplication by q^5. At a nonzero scalar root a the unique correction is b_+/(2a)-b_+^2/(8a^3), by cubically nilpotent truncation; there are two such a for every nonzero square scalar. In characteristic two the algebra is commutative with square-zero generators, and scalar Frobenius is bijective. The image count follows by adding all targets with nonzero square scalar component to J^3.

evidence: For degree-three u and degree-four s, conjugation by the unit 1+ell with ell in V sends u+s to u+s+2 ell wedge u; its inverse is 1-ell. For u nonzero, ell wedge u spans degree four. GL(V) acts transitively on nonzero cubic forms (all are decomposable in dimension four), and its determinant acts transitively on nonzero top forms.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Squaring commutes with each of these automorphisms, which preserve J. Thus all (q^4-1)q targets with nonzero cubic part form one orbit, and all q-1 pure nonzero top targets form another. Divide the earlier rank-two count by (q^4-1)q to get q^7(q^3-1), and the earlier rank-one count by q-1 to get the identical result since R4=q^2(q-1)(q^3-1). Summing the zero-square rows gives the zero fiber. The remaining cases are the usual scalar lifting in a nilpotent ideal and Frobenius in characteristic two. This is a direct implication even though the source does not label the two quotients as square-root counts.
